name: Windows Firewall Log
os_min: Windows XP (legacy pfirewall.log); Windows Vista+ for the Windows Firewall with Advanced Security event log channel
location: Legacy text log, must be manually enabled and is off by default: %windir%\System32\LogFiles\Firewall\pfirewall.log. Rule-change/administrative history: Applications and Services Logs\Microsoft-Windows-Windows Firewall With Advanced Security\Firewall (.evtx).
purpose: Records network traffic Windows Firewall evaluated (dropped and/or allowed connections, once logging is enabled) and, separately in the WFAS event channel, administrative changes to firewall rules and profile state — used to reconstruct blocked/allowed connection attempts and to detect firewall tampering.
key_fields: protocol, src-ip, dst-ip, src-port, dst-port, size
tcpflags, tcpsyn, tcpack, tcpwin, icmptype, icmpcode, info, path (W3C extended log fields in pfirewall.log)
Event ID 2004 (rule added) / 2005 (rule modified) / 2006 (rule deleted) in the WFAS Firewall event channel
normal_baseline: On a default installation pfirewall.log does not exist at all, because both dropped-packet and successful-connection logging are disabled by default on every profile (Domain/Private/Public). When enabled, entries reflect routine blocked broadcast/scan noise from the local segment plus a low, steady trickle of rule-change events tied to application installs.
anomalies: pfirewall.log present with DROP entries for outbound traffic to known-bad IPs/ports, or unexplained inbound ALLOW entries
A burst of Event ID 2004/2005/2006 entries around the time of an intrusion, especially rules opening high ports or allowing a specific unsigned binary
Firewall log file missing or truncated on a system where logging was known (via GPO) to be enabled, suggesting tampering
Log rolling off at its default 4096 KB cap during a long-dwell intrusion, losing early entries
parsing_tools: PowerShell Import-Csv / text viewer against pfirewall.log
SIEM ingestion (e.g. Microsoft Sentinel Windows Firewall connector)
anti_forensic_notes: Legacy pfirewall.log logging is off by default for both dropped and successful connections and must be explicitly enabled per network profile; an adversary with admin rights can disable logging, delete the file, or add/remove rules via netsh advfirewall, and the log itself is capped at a small rolling size (default 4096 KB / max 32767 KB, oldest entries deleted first), so its absence proves nothing about whether logging was ever on. The WFAS event log channel records rule-change events (2004/2005/2006) independently of whether text logging is enabled, though clearing that event log is itself recorded as a log-cleared event.
